criteria_quotes: Lumbar laminectomy for individuals with a herniated disc when all of the following criteria are met (see also Additional Notes section): All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out, including but not limited to significant pathology at other spinal level(s) on the advanced imaging radiology report that is/are not part of the surgical request resulting in incomplete surgical planning; and Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; and Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy Footnote1 * (unless there are indications for waiver of requirements for conservative management, noted below); and Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression;

Footnote1* Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression.

For elective laminectomy (cervical, thoracic, or lumbar) or spinal fusion (cervical, thoracic, or lumbar), conservative therapy requirements and nicotine cessation requirements are waived ONLY for persons with clinical findings of myelopathy (with symptoms), cauda equina syndrome, severe weakness (graded 4 minus or less on MRC scale) or progressive weakness, or an associated infection/tumor and/or acute fracture.

For elective laminectomy (cervical, lumbar, and thoracic), if member is diabetic, their HbA1c should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to surgery, unless there is an urgent indication for surgery (e.g., myelopathy, cauda equina syndrome), severe weakness (graded 4 minus or less on Medical Research Council [MRC] scale) or progressive weakness.
